summary: The Healthy Communities Act of 2026 makes several changes to health insurance premium tax credits, Medicaid coverage, Affordable Care Act open enrollment timelines, and anti-fraud rules for health insurance exchanges.

affected_groups.effect: Subject to updated premium tax credit calculations and sliding-scale cost shares based on household income tiers.
Treated as having an income at 100 percent of the poverty line with a 0 percent applicable percentage for the premium tax credit.
Subject to new verification processes for enrollments, stricter standards of conduct, audits, civil penalties ranging from $10,000 to $200,000, and criminal penalties for willful fraud.
Eligible for extended and modified temporary FMAP increases under specific conditions.

key_provisions: Modifies the premium tax credit sliding scale and eligibility percentages based on household income relative to the federal poverty line.

Establishes a special rule for individuals in the Medicaid coverage gap, treating them as having household income equal to 100 percent of the poverty line with a 0 percent applicable premium percentage.
Extends and increases certain temporary Federal Medical Assistance Percentage (FMAP) increases for state Medicaid plans.
Repeals certain health provisions from Public Law 119-21.
Codifies Affordable Care Act open enrollment period dates to run from November 1 to January 15 starting in calendar year 2026.
Establishes strict civil and criminal penalties, verification processes, and standards of conduct for agents, brokers, and marketing organizations to prevent fraudulent Exchange enrollments.
Requires the Secretary to check the Death Master File quarterly to remove deceased individuals from Exchange plans.
missing_information: Exact net federal cost or budgetary impact of the tax credit modifications and FMAP increases.
Detailed definitions or requirements of specific regulations to be promulgated by the Secretary.
